citeAs: Mo Li, Songyang Zhang, Taolin Zhang, Haodong Duan, Yunxin Liu, Kai Chen (2025). NeedleBench: Evaluating LLM Retrieval and Reasoning Across Varying Information Densities. Transactions on Machine Learning Research.
creator: Mo Li, Songyang Zhang, Taolin Zhang, Haodong Duan, Yunxin Liu, Kai Chen (Tsinghua University, Shanghai AI Laboratory)
description: NeedleBench is a comprehensive synthetic benchmark framework designed to assess retrieval and reasoning performance of large language models in bilingual long-context tasks with adaptive context lengths (e.g., 4k, 8k, 32k, 128k, 200k, 1000k, and beyond). It includes information-sparse tasks (Single-Needle Retrieval, Multi-Needle Retrieval, Multi-Needle Reasoning) and an information-dense task (Ancestral Trace Challenge), with key data points systematically embedded at varying depths to rigorously test models' capabilities in diverse settings.
name: NeedleBench
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: For error analysis of the ATC task, approximately 10% of observed errors were manually annotated, focusing on cases where the question type is "identifying the eldest ancestor." Error types identified include: Under-thinking (60.2%), Partial Understanding Error (12.9%), Instruction Following Error (7.5%), Repetitive Output (7.5%), Hallucination Error (7.5%), and Other Errors (4.5%). Additionally, false error rates caused by instruction-following errors (boxed format) were analyzed for small models (Qwen1.5-1.8B-Chat and Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct).
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The dataset is synthetically generated rather than human-annotated. For information-sparse tasks, ground truth answers are the synthetically inserted needle content, and evaluation uses a keyword-aware Exact Match metric. For the ATC task, ground truth answers are algorithmically computed from the constructed family structure (e.g., the eldest ancestor is name_1 in the generated chain). For error analysis, approximately 10% of observed errors from the ATC task were manually annotated by the authors to identify error types.
rai:dataBiases: The authors explicitly use synthetic data to mitigate prior-knowledge bias: needles are "synthetic, abstract, and fictional statements or relational facts, deliberately designed to avoid overlap with any real-world knowledge or pretraining data." The paper demonstrates that realistic (Wikipedia-based) benchmarks may be saturated due to memorization, with models achieving 50-80 percentage point higher scores on realistic vs. synthetic tasks. The ATC uses name randomization to prevent memorization. The paper also notes that most models show a performance gap between English and Chinese, with English typically higher, which may reflect pretraining data distribution biases.
rai:dataCollection: NeedleBench is a synthetic benchmark framework. The dataset is programmatically constructed: information-sparse tasks embed synthetic "needle" statements (fabricated facts and kinship relations) at varying depths within haystack text (Paul Graham Essays for English tasks, ChineseDomainModelingEval for Chinese tasks). The information-dense Ancestral Trace Challenge (ATC) is fully algorithmically generated using a systematic data generation algorithm that creates synthetic family relationship chains with randomized names, diverse relationship terms, and shuffled statements to eliminate positional bias.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: For English haystack (filler) content: Paul Graham Essays dataset (Kamradt, 2023). For Chinese haystack content: ChineseDomainModelingEval dataset (Wei et al., 2023). The "needles" (key information units) are synthetically generated abstract and fictional statements, not derived from real-world data.
rai:dataLimitations: NeedleBench is a synthetic benchmark and may not fully reflect the complexity of real-world tasks. The paper explicitly states: "NeedleBench is a synthetic benchmark and may not fully reflect the complexity of real-world tasks." The benchmark focuses on retrieval and reasoning over long contexts but does not cover all aspects of long-context understanding. The ATC task uses simplified family relationship structures that may not capture all forms of complex real-world reasoning.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For information-sparse tasks, synthetic needle statements are inserted at varying depths within haystack text at fixed distances. For the ATC task, relationship statements are shuffled to eliminate positional bias. Needle counts range from 2 to 512 to provide scalable complexity. Each configuration is repeated R=10 times to enhance result stability.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Token lengths are measured using the GPT-4 tokenizer. A buffer is subtracted from the target context length when generating each input to mitigate the risk of instruction truncation due to tokenizer discrepancies across different models. Needles are inserted at various depths within the haystack content to create test instances at specific context lengths (4k, 8k, 32k, 128k, 200k, 1000k, and beyond).
rai:dataSocialImpact: NeedleBench provides critical insights and targeted evaluation tools essential for understanding and improving the long-context capabilities of LLMs. By identifying the "under-thinking" phenomenon and other failure modes, it helps guide future research to improve LLM reasoning strategies. The benchmark supports development of more capable LLMs for real-world applications such as legal document retrieval, academic research, and business intelligence aggregation.
rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating long-context retrieval and reasoning capabilities of large language models; benchmarking LLMs on bilingual (English and Chinese) long-context tasks; assessing performance across varying information densities (sparse to dense); evaluating models on adaptive context lengths from 4k to 1M+ tokens; identifying failure modes such as "under-thinking" in reasoning models; comparing model architectures and scales on long-context tasks.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4 tokenizer (tiktoken, https://github.com/openai/tiktoken) is used to measure token lengths for all test instances.

null_reasons.rai:annotatorDemographics: Dataset is synthetically generated; no human annotators are used for labeling. Error analysis was done by the paper authors but no demographics are provided.
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: No annotation platform is used; the dataset is synthetically generated with algorithmic ground truth.
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: No discussion of missing data in the synthetic dataset construction process.
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: No timeframe for data collection is mentioned; the dataset is synthetically generated.
null_reasons.rai:dataImputationProtocol: No imputation protocol described; the dataset is synthetically generated with no missing values to impute.
null_reasons.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: No versioning or maintenance plan described beyond stating all codes and resources are publicly available at OpenCompass.
